title: 1949 London County Council election
summary: The closest of the post-war LCC elections. A Conservative recovery left the two main parties level on 64 elected seats each, with the Liberals holding the balance with a single seat. The Conservatives narrowly led the popular vote, but Labour retained control of the council with the help of its majority among the aldermen.
highlights: Labour and the Conservatives tie on 64 elected seats each
Conservatives narrowly win the popular vote (50.7%)
The Liberals win a single seat
Labour keeps control thanks to its majority among the aldermen

council.note: 129 directly elected councillors, plus aldermen chosen by the council. With the elected seats tied, Labour retained control through its majority among the aldermen. Seat shares are taken from Rallings & Thrasher's record of LCC results.
council.otherVotesNote: Under the multi-member bloc vote each elector had as many votes as seats to fill; minor-party totals and shares are as recorded in the Elections Centre compendium and contemporary press reports, whose percentage bases differ slightly.
